protocol: The model is a tree of priority lists that follows the taxonomy. A node whose fitting products share one label predicts it. A split node fits a backfilled priority list for the next base-71 digit of the label on the products under it: tags are ordered by the share of their products on their most common digit, with ties to the larger tag and then the tag name, each tag takes the most common digit of the products it heads, and a product with no fitted tag takes the node's most common digit. Each digit has a child fitted on the products that have it. Nodes at the depth limit and below fit a plain backfilled priority list at weight 71 for the whole remaining path, ordered by taxonomy association or by taxonomy spread on the products under the node. Limit zero is the plain list. The vote variants give each tag its most common digit and take the plurality, with ties to the smaller digit. The consistent variant fits each child only on the products its parent sends to it correctly. The shared-order variant uses the taxonomy-association order of the whole fitting fold at every node. The archived L1 logistic regression and neural network are compared on the same folds. Folds have equal weight.
